What Is a Proxy Server?
Why use a proxy? One big reason is privacy. The proxy hides your IP address (that unique number identifying your device) from the website, keeping your location and identity more private. It’s like using a P.O. box instead of sharing your home address.

Diagram: How a forward proxy hides your IP address when requesting a webpage.
What Is a Reverse Proxy?

Security: They hide the server’s IP address, making it harder for hackers to target. They also protect against attacks like DDoS (where attackers flood a server with traffic).
Load Balancing: They spread traffic across multiple servers to preve…

articles.description:
A practical breakdown of computer networking concepts I recently studied, explained in simple terms and real life analogies.
What Are Packets?
Packets are like envelopes that carry your data from one computer to another. Just like you can’t send a huge parcel at once through a delivery company, large data is broken into smaller chunks (packets), each labeled and sent across the network. These packets reassemble at the destination.
Serial Data Transfer
This is when data is sent one bit at a time over a single communication line, like people queueing to pass through a narrow hallway one after the other. It’s slower than parallel transfer but more reliable for long distances.
What Is a Virtual LAN (VLAN)?
A VLAN lets you divide a physical network into multiple smaller logical networks. Imagin…
